source_name: OTP Bank – Befektetési szolgáltatás hirdetmények (MiFID)
why_relevant: Investment-service hirdetmények track MiFID/Bszt.-driven changes and product withdrawals (e.g. the OTPdirekt securities-function withdrawal notice), i.e. supervision-driven service redesign.

source_name: OTP Group Investor Relations – announcements / regulatory filings
why_relevant: Issuer-level regulated disclosures (rendkívüli tájékoztatás, annual/interim reports, capital and risk reporting). OTP states it discharges disclosure duties on its own site, BÉT and the MNB publication site — so this is also a pointer to those two.

source_name: MBH Bank – Hirdetmények / Felügyeleti dosszié (üzletszabályzatok)
why_relevant: The 'felügyeleti dosszié' is the MNB-mandated public dossier: üzletszabályzatok, ÁSZF, hirdetmények in one place with effective dates. MBH's post-merger unilateral ÁSZF changes explicitly cite the legal basis (e.g. 2013. évi CXXXV. tv. 1.§(8)), making causal attribution easy.

source_name: MBH Bank – Befektetésekkel kapcsolatos tájékoztatások / közlemények
why_relevant: Investment-side customer notices and közlemények; complements the tariff dossier for Bszt./MiFID-driven changes.

source_name: MKB / MBH legacy – Felügyeleti dosszié and Befektetőknek: nyilvánosságra hozatali irányelvek
why_relevant: Legacy MKB brand pages still host the supervisory dossier and the Pillar 3 disclosure policy ('nyilvánosságra hozatali irányelvek'), plus historic CRR disclosure documents useful as a baseline for the merged MBH group.

source_name: MBH Befektetési Bank – kibocsátási program alaptájékoztató
why_relevant: Base prospectuses restate the regulatory environment, MREL/capital requirements and risk factors in prose — an unusually candid summary of which rules the issuer expects to bind it.

source_name: K&H Bank – magánszemélyek hirdetmények / díjjegyzékek
why_relevant: K&H publishes hirdetmény modifications with an explicit 'előzetes meghirdetés dátuma' and reason, giving clean lead-time data on regulation-driven repricing.

source_name: K&H Bank – archív hirdetmények (magánszemélyek / vállalkozások / vállalat)
why_relevant: Archives allow reconstruction of a multi-year change history — essential for measuring how fast each bank reacts to a given rule, without depending on our own crawl start date.

source_name: K&H Értékpapír – dokumentumok / kondíciós listák
why_relevant: Separate legal entity within the K&H/KBC group; investment-services terms react to Bszt./MiFID and MNB supervisory expectations independently of the bank.

source_name: Erste Bank Hungary – Üzletszabályzat és ÁSZF hub
why_relevant: Central entry to Erste's terms; Erste's ÁSZF states unilateral modifications take effect on the 16th day after publication — a directly usable notice-period parameter for deadline modelling.

source_name: Erste Bank Hungary – hirdetmény document frontend (gate.erstebank.hu)
why_relevant: The actual document repository behind Erste's terms: versioned PDFs of ÁSZF, üzletszabályzat and retail condition lists, addressed by opaque documentId GUIDs.

source_name: Erste Lakástakarék Zrt. – hirdetmények
why_relevant: Home-savings (LTP) is a heavily legislated product line; its hirdetmények are a sensitive indicator of subsidy/statutory changes.

source_name: UniCredit Bank Hungary – kondíciók és hirdetmények (corporate & municipal, incl. archive)
why_relevant: UniCredit publishes both current and 'hatályon kívüli' (superseded) condition lists with clear publication/effective date pairs in the file names — machine-friendly change tracking.

source_name: UniCredit Bank Hungary – Lakossági kondíciók változása (news notice)
why_relevant: Narrative page explaining why retail conditions change (bank operating conditions / legal requirements) — gives the stated causal reason, not just the numbers.

source_name: Raiffeisen Bank Zrt. – Díjak és kondíciók + archívum
why_relevant: Current and archived condition lists; Raiffeisen has historically issued explicit notices tying unilateral fee changes to financial transaction tax legislation.

source_name: Raiffeisen Bank – Ügyféltájékoztatás portal (ertesites-* change notices)
why_relevant: Dedicated customer-notification subdomain; individual 'Értesítés a ... módosításról' pages state announcement date and effective date (e.g. announced 2024-08-09, effective 2024-10-09) — the cleanest notice-period evidence found in this cell.

source_name: GRÁNIT Bank Nyrt. – hirdetmények
why_relevant: Fast-growing digital bank; its hirdetmények show how a digital-first player passes regulation into product terms, often faster than incumbents.

source_name: GRÁNIT Bank Nyrt. – BÉT issuer page / KIB filings
why_relevant: Gránit is BÉT-listed; the exchange's KIB store holds its regulated filings (IR contact, extraordinary announcements). BÉT is the canonical pointer for all listed HU banks (OTP, Gránit, MBH bonds).

source_name: MNB Közzétételek (OAM) – tőkepiaci közzétételi rendszer
why_relevant: The officially appointed mechanism (OAM) storing all regulated information from HU issuers, including the listed banks in this cell. Single choke point to catch any regulatory filing a bank publishes, independent of its own website design.

source_name: CIB Bank – Basel 3 nyilvánosságra hozatal (Pillar 3 report)
why_relevant: Adjacent regulated entity (outside the named seven but same peer group); its Pillar 3 report demonstrates the standard HU disclosure template and URL convention, useful as a comparator and as a pattern for locating peers' equivalents.

source_name: MNB – Tájékoztató a 575/2013/EU rendelet szerinti intézményi nyilvánosságrahozatali követelményekről
why_relevant: Supervisory guidance defining what banks must disclose and when; the schema against which each bank's Pillar 3 file can be checked, and a lead indicator of upcoming disclosure-template changes (EBA ITS 3.0).

source_name: MBH Jelzálogbank – Üzletszabályzatok, ÁSZF, Hirdetmények
why_relevant: Mortgage-bank subsidiary with its own terms; mortgage-funding adequacy (JMM) and covered-bond rules bite here first, separately from the parent bank's hirdetmények.

source_name: Magyar Bankszövetség (Hungarian Banking Association) — Hírek, aktualitások
why_relevant: The peak banking-sector interest body's running news/announcement stream, where it signals reactions to draft legislation, MNB measures and government policy affecting banks. Fastest-moving indicator of what the sector is fighting about.

source_name: Magyar Bankszövetség — Kiadványok / Publikációk, Jelentések, Kommunikék
why_relevant: Quarterly sector reports (jelentések) and communiqués carry the association's structured commentary on the regulatory environment, tax/levy burden and supervisory developments — longer-form than press releases and often the only public write-up of a consultation outcome.

source_name: Magyar Bankszövetség — English section (Hungarian Banking Association)
why_relevant: English mirror of the association's positioning, aimed at EU-level and foreign audiences. Useful for cross-checking terminology and for statements framed for Brussels rather than Budapest.

source_name: Magyar Bankszövetség — Szakmai kapcsolatok (EBF / EMF affiliations)
why_relevant: Names the European umbrella bodies the Hungarian association channels its lobbying through (European Banking Federation, European Mortgage Federation). Those umbrellas publish consultation responses that carry the Hungarian position upward — a reliable route to positions never published domestically.

source_name: European Banking Federation (EBF) — consultation responses and position papers
why_relevant: The EBF consolidates national banking associations' views (Hungary among its ~32 member associations) into formal consultation responses to the European Commission, EBA and others. Gives the EU-level framing that Hungarian banks help shape, and often precedes domestic transposition fights.
